name: Defence, the Abolition Regime, and Disaster Response
summary: Structure and strength of the Concord Service, doctrine and military ethics, command constraints, the Abolition verification regime, disaster response and the Serrance inversion, planetary defence, cyber defence, and intelligence.

units.time: civil hours or Elysian years as stated

posture.canonNote: The Concord maintains a service, not an army.
posture.proportionArgument: A civilization that spends eleven times more on rescuing people from storms than on the capacity to fight is making a claim about itself, and Elysians make it deliberately.

branches.name: Response Corps
branches.summary: Disaster response, rescue, medical, and engineering; 84% of the Service and mostly reservist.

branches.name: Orbital Guard
branches.summary: Space traffic, debris management, and orbital rescue.

branches.name: Cyber Defence Directorate
branches.summary: Defence of networks and public infrastructure against a non-state threat model.

branches.name: Planetary Defence Directorate
branches.summary: Detection and deflection of impacting bodies from the Tyrran Belt population.

branches.name: Verification Inspectorate
branches.summary: Enforcement of the Abolition; unannounced right of entry to any facility in any Region.

branches.name: Standing Force
branches.summary: The armed contingency component; 0.09% of GCP and untested since EY 1.

doctrine.statement: Early detection. Absorbed impact. Rapid restoration.
doctrine.rationale: Doctrine is about shortening the interval between a thing happening and the system noticing, and about building systems that bend rather than break.

ethics.name: The oath is to the Charter
ethics.summary: Not to the Concord, the Executive Board, or any person. Its operative clause is a duty to refuse.

ethics.name: Duty to refuse a manifestly unlawful order
ethics.summary: Absolute, individual, and carrying no penalty for good-faith refusal. The most-taught provision in Service formation, because the Cassian Incident was averted by one officer exercising exactly this duty over ninety seconds.

ethics.name: No autonomous lethal systems
ethics.summary: Target selection and the decision to use force require an identified human at every escalation point.

ethics.name: No automated escalation
ethics.summary: Systems may de-escalate automatically; they may never escalate.

ethics.name: No secret forces and no secret budget
ethics.summary: Every unit, strength, and funding line publishes; operational details may be withheld for a maximum of three years and then publish automatically.

ethics.name: Service members retain full Charter rights
ethics.summary: Including expression, association, and with narrow operational exceptions the right to organise.

ethics.name: No conscription
ethics.summary: Service is voluntary and the Charter forbids compulsion.

command.deploymentWithinRegionRequires: that Region's request, or an order of the Constitutional Court

abolition.name: The Abolition regime
abolition.summary: Verified dismantling of all strategic weapons, completed EY 34; Tier 1 entrenched and non-withdrawable even by a departing Region.

instruments.name: Material accounting
instruments.summary: Continuous accounting of fissile material, tritium inventories, and neutron sources across all 6,200 fusion plants.

instruments.name: Right of access
instruments.summary: Entry to any facility in any Region, without notice and without stating cause.

instruments.name: Pathogen oversight
instruments.summary: Joint with Biosecurity at all 41 Concord containment facilities and every licensed synthetic-biology site.

instruments.name: Orbital accounting
instruments.summary: Every object above 10 cm catalogued and attributed to an operator.

instruments.name: Publication
instruments.summary: All findings publish, including inconclusive ones and the Inspectorate's own access refusals.

dualUseProblem.statement: The Abolition removes the stockpile, not the capability, and makes reconstitution slow, visible, and criminal. It was never a guarantee that nobody could — it is an arrangement in which anyone who tried would be seen doing it by an inspectorate they cannot bar, while everyone else still had years to respond.

abolition.inspectorateSelfAssessment: Either the system working or the system not looking hard enough, and we cannot fully distinguish these.

disasterDoctrine.principle: For harm, a human must authorise. For protection, a human must cancel.
disasterDoctrine.asymmetryNote: Deliberately the mirror image of the Cassian rule: no system may escalate toward harm without a human deciding to, and no system may withhold protection while waiting for a human to decide.
disasterDoctrine.acknowledgedCost: False activations are frequent, expensive, and erode public patience; three Regions measure declining evacuation compliance, which is exactly the failure mode a cry-wolf system produces. The Concord publishes the statistics rather than raising thresholds, and canon does not claim this has fully worked.

vesperEvent.name: The Vesper Event
vesperEvent.summary: A 140-metre body identified on an impacting trajectory six years out; a gravity tractor placed in EY 264 and a kinetic impactor in EY 266 moved it to pass at 41,000 km in EY 268.
vesperEvent.canonNote: The Concord's most complete institutional success, taught alongside the Cassian Incident as the pair of events defining what the Concord thinks it is for: one catastrophe averted by refusing to act, one by acting decades ahead.

planetaryDefence.smallBodyMitigation: building standards and refuge capacity rather than detection
planetaryDefence.directorateSelfAssessment: An answer to the wrong question, offered because we have no answer to the right one.

cyberDefence.securityThroughSecrecyRejected: A system whose security depends on its secrecy is a system nobody has checked.
fallbackExamples: paper procedures in ports and hospitals

intelligence.publishedSelfAssessment: We would probably not see the next Kessander before it was used.
intelligence.refusalReasoning: A surveillance apparatus capable of finding one group is capable of finding anyone, and the Concord would rather be vulnerable to a rare catastrophe than to a permanent one.
intelligence.canonPosition: A deliberate, argued, and genuinely contested choice.

knownWeaknesses.name: Dual-use is unsolvable
knownWeaknesses.summary: Fusion infrastructure is reconstitution infrastructure; the regime buys time and visibility, not impossibility.

knownWeaknesses.name: The Inspectorate's own uncertainty
knownWeaknesses.summary: Seventeen findings, none of concealment, and the Inspectorate publicly declines to claim this proves absence.

knownWeaknesses.name: No contested experience
knownWeaknesses.summary: The Standing Force has not fought since EY 1; canon does not pretend simulation substitutes.

knownWeaknesses.name: A service optimised for disaster
knownWeaknesses.summary: If the Concord ever needed an army it would need years, and the arrangement assumes it would have them.

knownWeaknesses.name: Deployment veto cuts both ways
knownWeaknesses.summary: A Region in genuine constitutional breakdown could refuse the deployment that would help it, and only the Court could override — slowly.

knownWeaknesses.name: Publication versus operations
knownWeaknesses.summary: Full publication of units, strengths, and budgets is a real operational constraint; the Service has argued for exceptions roughly once a decade and never won one.

knownWeaknesses.name: Cry-wolf erosion
knownWeaknesses.summary: Automatic protective activation produces frequent false alarms; three Regions measure declining evacuation compliance, and raising thresholds is refused.

knownWeaknesses.name: Small-body blindness
knownWeaknesses.summary: Objects under 30 m are effectively undetectable and would destroy a city district.

knownWeaknesses.name: Intelligence cannot see the threat it fears
knownWeaknesses.summary: The Assessment Branch publishes annually that it would probably not detect the next engineered-pathogen group before use.

knownWeaknesses.name: Untested renunciation
knownWeaknesses.summary: The offensive-cyber renunciation is unilateral and has never been tested against a capable adversary.

knownWeaknesses.name: Reservist release is uneven
knownWeaknesses.summary: Statutory release at full pay is honoured at 91%; small employers in small Regions honour it least.

knownWeaknesses.name: Concord-tier operational inexperience
knownWeaknesses.summary: The Concord tier has led only eleven responses in a century, so its own competence is exercised mostly in drills.
